This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 & 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation.
SCCH-5 2

. The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 15.12.2019 at about 4.00 p.m. petitioner had been a cleaner in Eicher Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA- 13-B-6396 and the said lorry was driving by its driver on Vaniyambadi - Ambur, NH Road, Opp. Vinnamangalam Co-op. Ank, Vaniyambadi, Tamilnadu,
at that time, another Lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-23-BP-8233 came at high speed in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the road centre median, then it went to wrong/right side of the road and dashed against Tanker Lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-18-AK-8831 and also lorry in which petitioner was travelling.
Due to the said impact, petitioner sustained severe injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Ambur Government Hospital, after first aid, he was shifted to Vellore Government Hospital, wherein he took treatment inpatient, for which SCCH-5 he has spent an amount of Rs.1,50,000/- towards treatment, medicines, conveyance and other incidental expenses.
3. At the time of the accident he was aged about 23 years, hale and healthy, working as Canter Cleaner, thereby earning Rs.15,000/- p.m. and bata of Rs.200/- per day.
Due to this accident, he is not able to do his day-to-day activities, thereby he has lost his earnings.

Out of this accident crime No.662/2019 is registered against the driver of the lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-23-BP- 8233 before the Ambur Police for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337, 304(A) of IPC.
R1 is the owner R2 is insurer of the said lorry, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

Hence, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% p.a.
SCCH-5 4.
On service of notice, respondent No.1/owner has remained absent, hence placed exparte.

Respondent No.2/insurer has appeared and filed written statement and denied the issuance of policy in respect of lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-23-BP-8233 vide its policy No.VGC0445895000102 valid since 14.02.2019 to 13.02.2020.

Further submitted that, both the drivers of the vehicles in question were not holding valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident and the owner of the said offending lorry was not possessing valid FC and Permit to ply the vehicle on road.
There is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(b) of M.V.Act.

Further denied age, occupation and income of the petitioner, claim made by the petitioner is higher, hence his petition is not Shivakumar B.N vs Venkatesan.S on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45061148/
2 maintainable.

sentences.text: Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
SCCH-5 5.

On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, this court has framed the following:
::ISSUES::
1.

Whether Petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 15.12.2019 at about 4.00 p.m. near Vaniyambadi-Ambur, NH Road, Opp.
Vinnamangalam, Co-operative Bank, Vaniyambadi, Tamil Nadu, due to rash and negligent driving of Lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-23-BP-8233 and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so how much and from whom?
SCCH-5 3. What order or award?

6. In order to prove his case, Petitioner himself deposed his evidence as PW-1, examined Medical Record Officer at Unity Lifeline Hospital Pvt Ltd., by name Muniswamappa as PW-2 and marked 3 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.3 and closed his evidence.

On the other hand, legal Manager of respondent No.2 is examined as RW-1 and marked 2 documents as per Ex.R.1 and Ex.R.2 and closed his evidence.
7. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1 : In the Negative Issue No.2 : In the Negative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following:
SCCH-5 ::REASONS::
8. Issue No.1:- Admittedly to prove petitioner's case, petitioner is examined as PW-1 and he has not exhibited any documents, but he has examined Medical Record Officer at Unity Lifeline Hospital by name Muniswamappa as PW-2, through him 3 documents are got marked i.e., authorization letter is marked as Ex.P.1, MLC Extract is marked as Ex.P.2 and case sheet is marked as Ex.P.3.

Except these 3 documents, petitioner has not placed any substantial records such as FIR, mahazar, sketch, charge sheet, wound certificate, discharge summary, statement of witness etc., to believe about occurrence of the accident and causing of injuries to the petitioner in accident that occurred on 15.12.2019 at about 4.00 p.m. as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1, that means, except oral evidence SCCH-5 petitioner has not taken any endeavours to examine Doctor to prove the injuries Shivakumar B.N vs Venkatesan.S on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45061148/
3 caused to him,

Further as stated above, except MLC Extract and case sheet, he has not placed any other police documents to believe the involvement of respondent No.1 vehicle in the accident as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1.
9.

Under such circumstances, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioner has failed to prove that very accident is occurred due to negligency of driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-23-BP-8233 which belongs to respondent No.1 and he has sustained injuries in the alleged accident.
In the case on hand, respondent No.1 has not at all contested the petition inspite of service of notice.

Further Legal Manager of respondent No.2 is examined as RW-1 who has exhibited authorization letter marked as Ex.R.1 and copy of policy SCCH-5 marked as Ex.R.2, but his evidence is not helpful to the case of the petitioner.
Under such circumstances, petitioner has utterly failed to prove the issue No.1 in his favour.
For all these reasons, I have answered above Issue No.1 in the negative.
10. Issue No.2:- Inview of the findings given on issue No.1, question of discussion and giving findings on this issue No.2 does not arise.
Hence, without any further discussion, I have answered Issue No.2 in the negative.

11. Issue No.3: For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER::
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is hereby dismissed.
SCCH-5 Parties have to bear their own costs.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer directly on computer, typed by her, thereof is corrected and then pronounced by me in the Open Court on this the 4th day of October, 2024)
(MANJUNATHA K.P.) VIII ADDL.
JUDGE, COURT OF SMALL CAUSES & ACJM,
BENGALURU.
